provenance: Emission factors are cradle-to-gate (A1-A3) kgCO2e per kg of material as installed, per EN 15804 via GaBi (IPCC AR5). PRIMARY SOURCE since 2026-10-10: IFC India Construction Materials Database v1.0 (thinkstep for IFC/EU Eco-cities, Nov 2017, Table 16 GWP) for cement_opc 0.91, brick_clay 0.39, concrete_ready_mix 0.11, concrete_low_clinker_30ggbs 0.089 (nearest: 25% GGBS listing), steel_reinforcement 2.6, steel_rebar_eaf 0.83, river_sand/aggregate_rock 0.009 -- each carries its own ef_source. Steel context: BOF 2.8, DRI 2.1 (same table); the widely-copied 1.85 remains the WORLD crude average and is still rejected for Indian rebar. REMAINING ICE-global figures (no India-specific listing found): glass_float 1.2 (= IFC float glass 1.2, convergent), cement_ppc/psc/ggbs/lc3, 50% GGBS concrete 0.08 (no 50% listing), recycled rebar 0.45, msand 0.008. aluminium_recycled kept as listed. IFC lists no material literally named 'primary aluminium' (nearest: Aluminum ingot 31, a different allocation -- NOT adopted); aluminium_primary 20.88 comes from CEEW instead.
boundary: A1-A3 (cradle to gate). Excludes transport (A4) and construction waste (C2).

cement_opc.ef_source: IFC India Construction Materials Database v1.0 (2017), Table 16: 'Cement (ordinary Portland cement, OPC)', GWP A1-A3 per EN 15804 via GaBi. Replaces ICE-global 0.74 on 2026-10-10.
cement_opc.note: Direct process emissions. Cement is the single largest emissions source in an Indian RC building (~40% of embodied carbon in residential studies). MUST be collected from the BOQ separately from concrete. EF 0.91 = IFC India DB 'Cement (OPC)' (2017); see ef_source.

cement_ppc.note: Pozzolanic Portland Cement. Same workability, lower clinker factor.

cement_psc.note: Portland Supreme Cement. Slag-based, lowest-emission mainstream cement.

cement_ggbs.note: Blast-furnace slag cement. Essentially an allocation of an existing byproduct. Strongest single-carbon lever in a concrete mix.

calcined_clay_cement_lc3.note: LC3. ~40% lower CO2 than OPC, no new raw material, pilot-scale in India.

concrete_ready_mix.ef_source: IFC India Construction Materials Database v1.0 (2017), Table 16: 'Ready mix concrete with ordinary Portland cement (OPC)'. Replaces ICE-mid 0.15 on 2026-10-10.
concrete_ready_mix.note: Cited ~0.16 kgCO2/kg for standard-mix concrete. Note this figure assumes a typical cement content, so specifying it alongside a separate cement quantity can double-count binder emissions.

concrete_low_clinker_30ggbs.ef_source: IFC India DB v1.0 (2017), Table 16 nearest listed: 'Ready mix concrete with Portland slag cement (25% GGBS)' = 0.089. No 30% GGBS variant is listed (verified absent 2026-10-10); key retained for BOQ compatibility, value is the 25% figure, still below OPC 0.11 so the substitution incentive holds.

concrete_low_clinker_50ggbs.note: 50% GGBS replacement. Standard for GGBS-concrete in Indian institutional practice.

steel_reinforcement.ef_source: IFC India Construction Materials Database v1.0 (2017), Table 16: 'Steel reinforcement (steel rebar)'. Context entries: BOF Steel 2.8, DRI Steel 2.1. Replaces 2.3 (CEEW/IEEFA route-average reading) on 2026-10-10; the widely-copied 1.85 remains the WORLD crude average and is still rejected.
steel_reinforcement.note: Indian integrated BF-BOF route: ~2.3 tCO2e/t (range 1.8-3.2). GreenPro cites Indian industry average 2.2-2.5. The commonly quoted 1.85 is the WORLD crude-steel average and is too low for Indian rebar.

steel_rebar_eaf.ef_source: IFC India DB v1.0 (2017), Table 16: 'EAF Steel'. Replaces 0.7 secondary-EAF estimate on 2026-10-10.
steel_rebar_eaf.note: DRI-EAF route, ~1.4 t/t; secondary EAF ~0.7. Limited Indian rebar supply today.

brick_clay.ef_source: IFC India Construction Materials Database v1.0 (2017), Table 16: 'Brick (common/facing)', GWP A1-A3. Kiln variants listed 0.31-0.59; 0.39 is the common-facing figure. Replaces ICE-global 0.24 on 2026-10-10.
brick_clay.note: Common fired clay brick. EF 0.39 = IFC India DB 'Brick (common/facing)' (2017); kiln variants 0.31-0.59. Standard red brick.

fly_ash_brick.note: ~60% below fired clay. Utilises thermal power plant ash.

aac_block.note: Autoclaved aerated concrete. Autoclaving adds energy but per kg it beats fired brick.

hollow_concrete_block.note: HCC. Less material per m2 of wall.

river_sand.ef_source: IFC India DB v1.0 (2017), Table 16: 'Sand'. Carbon-negligible either way; the river-sand block is ecological/legal, not carbon.
river_sand.advisory_text: Riverbed sand in the Mula-Mutha basin. Low emission but high ecological cost: removes riverbed habitat and disrupts groundwater recharge. Not permissible here without MPCB sourcing evidence.

sand_unspecified.ef_note: Midpoint of river_sand (0.009, IFC India 'Sand') and manufactured_sand_msand (0.008). Emissions are near-identical either way; the difference between these two sources is ecological and legal, not carbon.
sand_unspecified.advisory_text: Sand is specified as 'sand' with no source given. Confirm whether this is riverbed sand (prohibited in the Mula-Mutha basin without MPCB sourcing evidence) or manufactured sand from a permitted quarry. The carbon difference is negligible; the legal and ecological difference is not.

manufactured_sand_msand.advisory_text: Certified manufactured sand from a permitted quarry or M-sand plant. Preferred substitute for riverbed sand.

aggregate_rock.ef_source: IFC India DB v1.0 (2017), Table 16: 'Aggregate (mixed gravel/crushed stone)'. Replaces 0.005 rock-quarrying estimate on 2026-10-10.

aggregate_recycled.note: Recycled concrete aggregate. Requires contamination-free demolition input.

glass_low_e.note: Slightly higher embodied carbon but cuts operational cooling. Net benefit depends on climate and cooling load; surface this trade-off rather than treating it as a free win.

aluminium_primary.ef_source: CEEW Indian aluminium industry average (captive-coal smelters). Adopted 2026-10-10 replacing ICE-global virgin 12.5, which understated Indian smelter carbon ~40%. IFC India DB lists no primary-aluminium entry (ingot 31 is a different allocation, NOT adopted). Facade-heavy BOQs were undercounting carbon before this fix.
aluminium_primary.note: Primary aluminium is electrolysis-intensive. Dominates façade carbon.

aluminium_recycled.note: Recycled aluminium requires ~5% of the energy of primary. Largest single substitution win available in a façade.

timber_wood.note: Biogenic A1-A3 only. Note: stored-carbon benefits are NOT counted here; this factor is deliberately conservative and excludes biogenic credit.

tiles_vitrified.note: Marginal per-kg difference; the win from vitrified tile is thinner-set/dry-lay material saving, not the tile itself.

paint_emulsion.note: VOC-free low-emission paint. Included for completeness.

insulation_mineral.note: Embodied vs operational trade-off, same class as low-e glass.

insulation_xps.note: Very high due to blowing agents. Large penalised use of XPS raises a project's total despite good thermal performance.

laterite.ef_basis: Derived from aggregate_rock (0.009, IFC India), not independently measured in India. Quarrying, crushing and hauling only -- no calcination, so the emissions are transport-dominated and near-negligible against cement and steel. Marked ESTIMATE: a published Indian factor would supersede this.
laterite.note: Laterite stone. PMC-area filler and sub-base.

trap_rock.ef_basis: Derived from aggregate_rock (0.009, IFC India), not independently measured in India. Quarrying, crushing and hauling only -- no calcination, so the emissions are transport-dominated and near-negligible against cement and steel. Marked ESTIMATE: a published Indian factor would supersede this.
trap_rock.note: Deccan basalt. Standard PMC building stone.

aggregate_ggi.ef_basis: Derived from aggregate_rock (0.009, IFC India), not independently measured in India. Quarrying, crushing and hauling only -- no calcination, so the emissions are transport-dominated and near-negligible against cement and steel. Marked ESTIMATE: a published Indian factor would supersede this.

murrum.ef_basis: Derived from aggregate_rock (0.009, IFC India), not independently measured in India. Quarrying, crushing and hauling only -- no calcination, so the emissions are transport-dominated and near-negligible against cement and steel. Marked ESTIMATE: a published Indian factor would supersede this.

cupleted_soil.ef_basis: Derived from aggregate_rock (0.009, IFC India), not independently measured in India. Quarrying, crushing and hauling only -- no calcination, so the emissions are transport-dominated and near-negligible against cement and steel. Marked ESTIMATE: a published Indian factor would supersede this.
cupleted_soil.note: Cupleted/soil mix. Excavated material reused on site.

stabilized_earth_block_seb.ef_basis: Cement-stabilised earth block: predominantly the cement binder. Scaled from brick_clay (0.24) by the cement fraction and a nominal stabiliser dose. Marked ESTIMATE.
stabilized_earth_block_seb.note: Cement stabilised earth block. Low-carbon masonry alternative.

carbon_intensity_bands.note: Breakpoints are UNSOURCED house bands inherited from Deepesh's config. Do not attribute them to GRIHA. Sourced anchors are in config/regions/pune.json under carbon.source_anchors: IGBC Near Net Zero <= 700 kgCO2e/m2, observed Indian high-rise residential mean 454 (range 373-530).
